summary: A 1977 Telnet option for the SUPDUP protocol, letting a Telnet connection switch to SUPDUP mode. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo defines a Telnet option for switching a connection to the SUPDUP display protocol. The hosts negotiate first, and the option is off unless they agree.

questions: what is the telnet supdup option
what is the telnet option code for supdup
subtitle: A Telnet option for agreeing to use the SUPDUP display protocol.

tldr.problem: A Telnet connection needed a way for its two hosts to agree to use SUPDUP display service.
tldr.mechanism: The SUPDUP option, code 21, uses Telnet WILL, WON'T, DO and DON'T commands to request, accept or refuse the option.
tldr.outcome: SUPDUP is off by default; after both sides accept, communication proceeds using SUPDUP rules.

today: RFC 736 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The SUPDUP Option
sections.content: RFC 736 assigns the Telnet option name SUPDUP the code 21. The option lets a host offer SUPDUP terminal service over the normal Telnet socket instead of the normal SUPDUP ICP socket. It is a negotiation mechanism; the SUPDUP protocol itself is described elsewhere.
sections.plainLanguage: The option gives Telnet a named signal for requesting SUPDUP display service. It lets the hosts decide whether to use that service on their connection.

sections.title: How the Hosts Agree
sections.content:
A user Telnet program that wants SUPDUP sends IAC DO SUPDUP. A willing server replies with IAC WILL SUPDUP; otherwise it refuses with IAC WON'T SUPDUP. A server that normally provides SUPDUP may offer the option when the initial connection protocol begins, and the user may accept or refuse.

Once the option is active, the RFC says no further Telnet negotiations are allowed because SUPDUP has its own facilities for needed functions. SUPDUP negotiation then proceeds as described in RFC 734.
sections.plainLanguage: The user side asks to use SUPDUP, and the server accepts or refuses. Once both accept, they use SUPDUP's own rules instead of negotiating more Telnet options.

sections.title: The Default State
sections.content: The default is WON'T SUPDUP and DON'T SUPDUP. In that state, the SUPDUP display protocol is not in use. The option takes effect only after negotiation.
sections.plainLanguage: SUPDUP does not start automatically. The connection stays outside SUPDUP unless the hosts agree to turn the option on.

references.text: The SUPDUP display protocol, referenced by RFC 736.
